nodes.name: Grama grasses
nodes.desc: Blue grama, black grama and relatives dominate the desert grasslands of the Chihuahuan Desert, the grass layer that seed-eaters and grazers rely on.

nodes.name: Apache plume
nodes.desc: A shrub of rocky slopes and washes, among the most recorded plants near the park. GloBI records show mule deer eating it.

nodes.name: Pinyon pine
nodes.desc: Grows with juniper on the lower eastern slopes. Its seeds are eaten by rock squirrels in GloBI records.

nodes.name: Chinkapin oak
nodes.desc: Grows in canyon bottoms such as McKittrick, where Wikipedia says the trees depend on spring water. Its acorns are food for squirrels and mice.

nodes.name: Prickly pear
nodes.desc: Cactus pads and fruit are abundant on desert slopes and uplands and give moisture and food to animals such as peccaries.

nodes.name: Mule deer
nodes.desc: The best recorded large mammal near the park. It browses shrubs such as Apache plume and is a main prey of the cougar.

nodes.name: Elk
nodes.desc: Listed among the large mammals of the park. Grasses are a year-round staple of elk diet, and cougars are among their predators.

nodes.name: Collared peccary
nodes.desc: Called javelina locally. Feeds on cactus such as prickly pear and is taken by cougars and eaten as carrion by vultures in GloBI records.

nodes.name: Merriam's kangaroo rat
nodes.desc: A small desert rodent that mostly eats seeds, including grass seeds. Snakes and coyotes hunt it.

nodes.name: Rock squirrel
nodes.desc: Eats seeds and nuts such as pinyon seeds, and is prey of cougars, rattlesnakes, bullsnakes and eagles.

nodes.name: Deer mouse
nodes.desc: One of many mice of the park. Eats seeds and insects, and is a common prey of snakes.

nodes.name: White-winged dove
nodes.desc: A seed- and fruit-eating bird of desert scrub. GloBI records show rattlesnakes and bullsnakes eating it.

nodes.name: Western diamond-backed rattlesnake
nodes.desc: Ambushes kangaroo rats, mice, squirrels and birds, according to GloBI records.

nodes.name: Bullsnake
nodes.desc: A large constrictor that eats rodents and birds. GloBI records include kangaroo rats, mice and doves.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: Scavenges carcasses of deer, peccary and squirrels, and so returns dead matter to the food web.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: Listed among the park's carnivores. Eats rodents and also feeds on carrion.

nodes.name: Cougar
nodes.desc: The top predator. Mule deer are a main prey; GloBI records also show it taking peccary and rock squirrels, and elk are known prey.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: A raptor of cliffs and open country in the park. Takes ground squirrels and other small animals.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong sun and heat drive desert plant growth and also dry the ground.

nodes.name: Monsoon rain
nodes.desc: Most rain falls from late June to early October with the summer monsoon, in a desert averaging about 235 mm a year.

nodes.name: Canyon springs
nodes.desc: The range is mostly limestone with little surface water, so seeps, springs and McKittrick Creek sustain the canyon trees.

nodes.name: Soil nutrients
nodes.desc: Thin limestone soils hold nutrients that plants take up.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and insects break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil.
